entries.claim: Statcounter shows Vietnam's mobile web traffic at Android 57.33% and iOS 42.64% in August 2026, a lower Android share than the 65-70% quoted by two vendors.
entries.appliesWhen: Web-traffic share; game revenue split not measured.

support.excerpt: Aug 2026: Android 57.33%, iOS 42.64%.

counterSupport.excerpt: Android dominates with almost 70% of the market share in Vietnam.
Vendor states Android 65% / iOS 35% (older, unsourced figure).

entries.useFor: Vietnam's iOS share is large enough that App Store parity matters more than in ID/PH.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor figures are older (AppTweak Feb 2024: almost 70% Android; LocalizeDirect Oct 2024: 65/35) and unsourced.

entries.claim: Vietnam ranked third in Southeast Asian game downloads in Q1 2025 with 329 million, behind Indonesia (870M) and the Philippines (366M).
entries.appliesWhen: Sensor Tower download estimates, both stores.

support.excerpt: The Philippines and Vietnam follow with 366 million and 329 million downloads respectively.

entries.useFor: Vietnam is a high-volume install market.
entries.researcherNote: Single origin.

entries.claim: Vietnam's Decree 147/2024 took effect on 25 December 2024 and requires offshore entities providing online games to Vietnamese users to establish an enterprise in Vietnam.
entries.appliesWhen: Publishers offering online games to Vietnam users.

support.excerpt: Offshore entities providing online game services to users in Vietnam must establish an enterprise in compliance with the decree.
Offshore game publishers must establish a local entity in Vietnam to operate legally.
Decree effective December 25, 2024 following its November 9th issuance.

entries.useFor: Vietnam release needs a local entity; treat any Vietnam store creative as gated on licensing.
entries.researcherNote: Three law-firm/trade summaries of the same decree (one origin); decree text not read, and the government-portal page was not re-fetched.

entries.claim: Vietnam splits online games into G1 (multiplayer via central servers, needing a licence and a Decision to Publish) and G2-G4 (needing a Notice of Publishing Confirmation).
entries.appliesWhen: Online games under Decree 147.

support.excerpt: G1 titles need a Decision to Publish and G2, G3, and G4 games require a Notice of Publishing Confirmation.
Government decisions/notifications required per tier (Tilleke summary).

entries.useFor: Identify the tier before any Vietnam creative work.
entries.researcherNote: Secondary sources; tier for Rogue Legend must be determined with counsel.

entries.claim: Decree 147 bars advertising an online game in Vietnam without a G1 release decision or a G2-G4 notification confirmation.
entries.appliesWhen: Any advertising of an online game to Vietnam users; whether pre-registration store pages count as advertising is not settled by the sources.

support.excerpt: Not advertising online games without a decision on G1 game release or notification confirmation of G2, G3, or G4 game release.
Businesses cannot advertise games without proper authorization documentation.

entries.useFor: Do not run Vietnam store creative or pre-registration before the licence document exists.
entries.researcherNote: Two secondary sources, one decree (one origin). Enforcement against store pages not verified.

entries.claim: Decree 147 requires game classification results to be displayed continuously on the game screen and in advertising content, as a symbol of recognisable size and colour.
entries.appliesWhen: Online games offered in Vietnam; paraphrase of 'recognizable size and colour' comes from the same page.

support.excerpt: Hiển thị liên tục kết quả phân loại trò chơi trong màn hình thiết bị trò chơi và trong các nội dung quảng cáo.

entries.useFor: Reserve space for a Vietnamese age mark in any Vietnam ad or store graphic.
entries.researcherNote: One fetched source (Vietnamese); a second (Tilleke) mentions the display on the provider's website only. Whether Play screenshots count as advertising content is unverified.

entries.claim: Decree 147 classifies online games into four age tiers (all ages, 12+, 16+, 18+), but sources disagree whether the lowest tier is labelled 00+ or 6+.
entries.appliesWhen: Age labelling of Vietnam releases.

support.excerpt: Four categories: 00+ (all ages), 12+, 16+, 18+.
New age rating introduced for users 16+.

counterSupport.excerpt: Search summary lists the tiers as 6+, 12+, 16+, 18+ (Article 38); page not fetched.

entries.useFor: Confirm the exact label set from the decree before designing the mark.
entries.researcherNote: Contradiction: a search summary of thuvienphapluat.vn (page returned HTTP 403, not fetched) lists 6+/12+/16+/18+. Verify against the decree.

entries.claim: In August 2026 Ho Chi Minh City's Department of Culture and Sports told publishers that games approved as 18+ must not be shown as 12+ or 13+ on app stores, with 15 days to correct or risk distribution suspension.
entries.appliesWhen: Games with an official Vietnamese age approval; consequences: distribution suspension or revoked publishing approval.

support.excerpt: Games officially approved for players aged 18 and above must not be displayed as suitable for younger audiences, such as 12+ or 13+, on app stores.

entries.useFor: Vietnam store age rating must equal the approved Vietnamese classification.
entries.researcherNote: One news report (5 Aug 2026 per page), one origin. This is the only found instance of Vietnamese authorities directing app-store age labels.

entries.claim: Decree 147 prohibits online games with content and scenarios resembling casino prize games or using images of playing cards.
entries.appliesWhen: Games released in Vietnam.

support.excerpt: Prohibit the release of online games that feature content and scenarios resembling prizewinning games in casinos or games using images of playing cards.

entries.useFor: Avoid casino or playing-card imagery in Vietnam-facing art.
entries.researcherNote: Secondary source. Not directly aimed at store images but the same imagery would be a risk.

entries.claim: For 12+ games, Decree 147 requires no suggestive material and limits combat to animated, non-human or unrealistic human depictions with non-realistic weapons.
entries.appliesWhen: Games classified 12+.

support.excerpt: animated, non-human or unrealistic human portrayals, with non-realistic weapons, minimal close-up effects, and restrained sounds.

entries.useFor: Cartoon combat art fits a 12+ tier; realistic or suggestive art pushes the tier up.
entries.researcherNote: One trade-press summary of the decree.

entries.claim: Under Decree 147 foreign app stores must remove illegal applications within 24 hours of a written request and verify that game providers hold valid approval certificates before upload.
entries.appliesWhen: Google Play and App Store as foreign app stores.

support.excerpt: Foreign app stores must 'remove illegal applications within 24 hours' and verify online game providers hold valid approval certificates before upload.
Platform providers must remove violating applications upon authorized request.

entries.useFor: An unlicensed game can be delisted in Vietnam.
entries.researcherNote: Two law/trade summaries of one decree.

entries.claim: An analysis piece says 288 Vietnamese G1 licences had been issued by Q1 2026 and only 184 remained active, a 36% revocation rate.
entries.appliesWhen: G1 licences.

support.excerpt: As of Q1 2026, 288 G1 licences have been issued with only 184 remaining active - a 36% revocation rate.

entries.useFor: Suggests active enforcement, but unverified.
entries.researcherNote: No named primary source for the numbers.

entries.claim: On 2026-09-29 Capybara Go, Archero 2 and Survivor.io returned HTTP 404 on Google Play with gl=VN (in both vi and en); Capybara Go resolved for Singapore and Malaysia, and Legend of Mushroom was available in Vietnam.
entries.appliesWhen: Fetched anonymously from a non-Vietnamese IP; Habby games are not listed for Vietnam.

support.excerpt: com.habby.capybara, com.xq.archeroii, com.dxx.firenow: 404 at gl=VN; com.mxdzzus.google: 200 at gl=VN.

entries.useFor: The three Habby competitors are not served in Vietnam; Vietnam competition is local publishers and Legend of Mushroom.
entries.researcherNote: Fact is an observation; the cause (Decree 147 licensing, publisher choice) is not established. Singapore/Malaysia check done for Capybara Go only.

entries.claim: In the 22 top-grossing games on Vietnam Google Play (26 Sep 2026 chart), the first phone screenshot set was landscape in 15 and portrait in 7; the median was 7 screenshots (range 5 to 8).
entries.appliesWhen: Top-grossing games of all genres in Vietnam.

support.excerpt: 15 landscape, 7 portrait; median 7; range 5 to 8.

entries.useFor: Landscape is the local top-grossing norm, driven by MOBA/MMO/strategy genres.
entries.researcherNote: Chart order from Similarweb (used only to pick packages). Single snapshot of one chart on one day; chart mix is dominated by Vietnam-published MMO, MOBA and casual titles, not roguelikes.

entries.claim: All six viewed Vietnam top-grossing listings (Lien Quan Mobile, OMG 3Q, Rise of Kingdoms VN, Thu Cung Bao Dan, Play Together VNG, Wild Rift VN) use Vietnamese captions on their screenshots.
entries.appliesWhen: Mostly Vietnam-published titles (local partner listings) in the top-grossing chart.

support.excerpt: Vietnamese captions on all six viewed listings.

entries.useFor: Vietnamese captions are the norm; English-only screenshots are unusual among locally published leaders.
entries.researcherNote: Six hand-picked listings, all locally published.

entries.claim: In viewed Vietnam listings, headlines often carry a Vietnamese sub-line (Thu Cung Bao Dan, Rise of Kingdoms, Play Together), while OMG 3Q pairs bold headlines with name-labelled real-person portraits.
entries.appliesWhen: Viewed listings only; density judged by eye.

support.excerpt: Two-tier Vietnamese captions in Thu Cung Bao Dan, Rise of Kingdoms and Play Together; OMG 3Q shows name-labelled real-person portraits in five of six screenshots.

entries.useFor: Two-line Vietnamese captions and human-face endorsers are locally normal.
entries.researcherNote: Stylistic observation from six listings.

entries.claim: Local celebrities appear in Vietnamese game promotion: a vendor cites footballer Doan Van Hau accompanying Call of Dragons announcements, and OMG 3Q's Play screenshots feature name-labelled real people.
entries.appliesWhen: Vietnam game marketing; store-image effect not measured.

support.excerpt: famous Vietnamese footballer Doan Van Hau accompanied announcements of the Call of Dragons game.
OMG 3Q screenshots 2 to 6 show named real-person portraits.

entries.useFor: Endorser portraits are a local option; test as a variant, not a default.
entries.researcherNote: Two origins but only one store-image example; the people in OMG 3Q were not identified as KOLs by the listing.

entries.claim: Publisher gift codes are a mainstream Vietnamese game marketing mechanic: aggregator GameK lists launch and event codes (newest 16 Sep 2026), and Legend of Mushroom's Vietnam listing shows a gift code in its first screenshot.
entries.appliesWhen: Vietnam PC/mobile game marketing.

support.excerpt: Aggregator page lists gift codes for many games; newest dated 2026-09-16.
Legend of Mushroom vi listing screenshot 1 shows 'Gift Code: ANNIV2P5'.

entries.useFor: Gift codes are a familiar Vietnamese hook, but keep them out of store graphics unless policy allows.
entries.researcherNote: Two origins; promotional codes in Play graphics may conflict with Play's graphic policy (see Play policy entries).

entries.claim: Vietnamese text typically needs about 30% more space than English (30-35% per AppTweak, about 30% per LocalizeDirect).
entries.appliesWhen: English-to-Vietnamese caption translation.

support.excerpt: Expect a 30-35% increase in space requirements when converting from English.
Text typically expands approximately 30% compared to English.

entries.useFor: Leave 30-35% caption room in the caption band.
entries.researcherNote: Two vendors, likely both rule-of-thumb; not a measurement.

entries.claim: Vietnamese diacritics stack on a single letter and change meaning (bạn 'friend' vs bắn 'shoot'), so caption fonts must support the full Vietnamese set.
entries.appliesWhen: Any baked-in Vietnamese text.

support.excerpt: Many Vietnamese words take on a completely different meaning when their accent is changed - bạn vs bắn.
Multiple diacritical symbols can be stacked on a single letter.

entries.useFor: Check every caption in a Vietnamese-capable display font and have a native review.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor sources; the font-support part is an inference. Test on real captions.

entries.claim: AppTweak describes Vietnamese game creatives as more crowded than apps, with elaborate illustrations and characters prominently displayed.
entries.appliesWhen: Observational, no data; last updated 2024-02.

support.excerpt: Games: more crowded designs with elaborate illustrations and characters prominently displayed.

entries.useFor: Character-forward, busy art is locally normal.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor description; consistent with the viewed OMG 3Q and Rise of Kingdoms listings but not measured.

entries.claim: Vietnam scores 500 in EF EPI 2025 (64th globally, Moderate band).
entries.appliesWhen: General adult population.

support.excerpt: Vietnam recorded 500, reflecting moderate proficiency levels.

entries.useFor: English brand terms may pass, but captions are localised by the local leaders.
entries.researcherNote: EF test-taker samples.
